paper.title: The Intrinsic Robustness of Stochastic Bandits to Strategic Manipulation

settings.name_in_paper: Strategic manipulations in stochastic bandits (UCB principal)
unmapped: Manipulation budget is per arm: arm i has total budget B_i with sum_t |alpha_t^(i)| <= B_i
The optimal arm cannot be manipulated (B_{i*} = 0)
Each arm can only manipulate its own reward when pulled, adaptively based on its own history
settings.definition_quote: when $I_t = i$, arm $i$ can add an additional reward amount $\alpha_t^{(i)}$ to the realized reward $r_t$, subject to budget constraint $\sum_{t = 1}^T |\alpha_t^{(i)} | \leq B_i$, so that the revealed reward to the principal is $\widetilde{r_t} = r_t + \alpha_t^{(i)}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Strategic manipulations in stochastic bandits (epsilon-Greedy principal)
unmapped: The optimal arm cannot be manipulated (B_{i*} = 0)
settings.definition_quote: When $I_t = i$, arm $i$ can add an additional reward amount $\alpha_t^{(i)}$ ... subject to budget constraint $\sum_{t = 1}^T |\alpha_t^{(i)} | \leq B_i$

settings.name_in_paper: Strategic manipulations in stochastic bandits (Thompson Sampling principal)
unmapped: The optimal arm cannot be manipulated (B_{i*} = 0)
settings.definition_quote: When $I_t = i$, arm $i$ can add an additional reward amount $\alpha_t^{(i)}$ ... subject to budget constraint $\sum_{t = 1}^T |\alpha_t^{(i)} | \leq B_i$

settings.name_in_paper: Strategic manipulations in stochastic bandits, LSI manipulation (lower bound)
unmapped: Arms play the Lump Sum Investing (LSI) strategy (a dominant-strategy SPE for UCB)
settings.definition_quote: {\bf \lsi manipulation. } A particular manipulation strategy that will be of interest is the \emph{Lump Sum Investing} ($\mathtt{LSI}$) strategy, in which an arm simply spends all of its remaining budget whenever first pulled.

conditions: arbitrary adaptive manipulation strategy of the non-optimal arms

source.label: thm:ucb-ub
source.quote: For any manipulation strategy $S$ of the strategic arms, the regret of the UCB principal is bounded by \E[R(T)] \leq \sum_{i\neq i^*} \big[\max\left\{3B_i, \frac{81\sigma^2\ln T}{\Delta_i} \right\} +\big(1 + \new{3}\Delta_i \big]

results.notes: Printed bracket is unbalanced ('(1 + 3\Delta_i'); Lemma 3.2 times Delta_i gives max{...}+3Delta_i, so the reading 1+3Delta_i is valid. Regret defined as sum Delta_i E[n_i(T)] (pseudo-regret w.r.t. true rewards).

source.label: lem:ucb-ub
source.quote: Suppose the principal runs UCB. For any manipulation strategy $S$ of strategic arms, the expected number of times that arm $i (i\neq i^*)$ is pulled up to time $T$ can be bounded as follows, \E[n_i(T)] \leq \max\left\{\frac{3B_i}{\Delta_i}, \frac{81\sigma^2\ln T}{\Delta_i^2} \right\} + 3

results.notes: Bound on expected number of pulls E[n_i(T)] of a suboptimal arm.

symbols.c_0: unspecified constant hidden in the O(.) term (depends on sigma)

conditions: each strategic arm uses the LSI strategy (dominant-strategy SPE)

source.label: thm:ucb-egreedy-lb
source.quote: Suppose the principal uses UCB algorithm and each arm uses $\mathtt{LSI}$. For any $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian reward distributions on arms, the regret of the principal satisfies, \E[R(T)] \geq \underline{\Delta}\sum_{i\neq i^*} \frac{B_i}{2\Delta_i} - \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{\ln T}{\underline{\Delta}}\right).

results.notes: Algorithm-specific lower bound for UCB under LSI. Proof gives the subtracted term as Delta_min*(36 sigma^2 ln T/Delta_min^2 + 1 + 2(K-1)/T). Theorem 3.5 reduces this to bounded rewards with LSIBR at an additional loss O(Delta_min ln T/(1-mu_star)^2) (not recorded separately).

symbols.c_0: unspecified constant hidden in the O(.) term (depends on c, K, sigma)

source.label: thm:e-greedy-ub
source.quote: For any adaptive manipulation strategy $S$ of strategic arms, the regret of the $\vareps$-Greedy principal with $\eps_t = \min\{1, \frac{cK}{t}\}$ and $c = \max\{20, \frac{36\sigma^2}{\underline{\Delta}}\}$, is bounded by \E[R(T)] \leq \sum_{i \neq i^*}\big[3B_i  + \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{\ln T}{\Delta_i}\right)\big].

results.notes: The O(.) hides constants depending on c and K. Algorithm does not use T, so anytime. Supporting Lemma C.1 bounds E[n_i(T)] <= 3B_i/Delta_i + O(ln T/Delta_i^2).

symbols.c_0: unspecified constant hidden in the O(.) term

source.label: thm:ts-ub
source.quote: For any manipulation strategy profile $S$ of strategic arms, the regret of the Thompson Sampling principal can be bounded as \E[R(T)] \leq \sum_{i\neq i^*} \max\Big\{6B_i, \frac{72\sigma^2\ln T}{\Delta_i}\Big\} + \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{\ln T}{\Delta_i}\right).

results.notes: O-term placement read as inside the sum over suboptimal arms. Constant may depend on sigma (e^{11/(4 sigma^2)} factors in proof).

symbols.c_0: unspecified constant hidden in the O(.) term

source.label: lem:ts-ub
source.quote: For any manipulation strategy profile $S$, the expected number of times that arm $i$ is pulled up to time $T$ can be bounded as follows: \E[n_{i}(T)] \leq \max\Big\{\frac{6B_i}{\Delta_i}, \frac{72\sigma^2\ln T}{\Delta_i^2}\Big\} + \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{\ln T}{\Delta_i^2}\right).

results.notes: Bound on expected pull count of suboptimal arm.

symbols.c_0: unspecified constant hidden in the O(.) term

conditions: principal runs epsilon-Greedy (eps_t = min{1, cK/t}, c = max{20, 36 sigma^2/Delta_min}) or Thompson Sampling

source.label: prop:ts-lb
source.quote: Suppose the principal runs \egreedy{} or Thompson Sampling and each strategic arm uses $\mathtt{LSI}$. For any $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian reward distributions on arms, the regret of the principal satisfies, \E[R(T)] \geq \underline{\Delta}\sum_{i\neq i^*}\frac{B_i}{2\Delta_i} - \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{\ln T}{\underline{\Delta}}\right).

results.notes: Lower bound for specific algorithms (epsilon-Greedy and TS) under LSI manipulation; not necessarily an equilibrium.
